claim: Not the smallest fix, and not because of the shape the brief proposes: the guard carries a conjunct that cannot change the outcome. `askedThisTurn` only ever holds `null` or a string (line 471, `data.question || ""`), and this branch is reachable only when `data.final_message` is truthy, i.e. a non-null string. For every such value, `data.final_message === null` is false, so `!(askedThisTurn !== null && data.final_message === askedThisTurn)` and `!(data.final_message === askedThisTurn)` are the same predicate. Measured: with the conjunct deleted, all 7 scenarios produce byte-identical output (see premise). The brief's alternative — never render when an ask_user frame was seen, `data.final_message && !askedThisTurn` — is also fewer conditions and would be correct, but it is the wrong direction: it keeps the new global. P2 gives the form with no new state at all: `} else if (data.final_message && data.final_message !== curRaw) {`. This item is chars, not lines: the condition stays one line either way.

quote: let askedThisTurn = null;  // question already rendered by an ask_user frame, or null
claim: Redundant with `curRaw`, which already means exactly this at the point the guard runs. In the ask_user branch (lines 466-471) the code does `curRaw = data.question || ""`, then `renderCurrent()`, then `closeText()`; `closeText()` is `curTextEl = null` and nothing else (line 342), so when the following `done` frame arrives the UI still holds the rendered question in `curRaw`. The new global stores the same string from the same payload, one line apart. Measured: swapping the predicate for `data.final_message !== curRaw` changes no rendered output in any of the 7 scenarios, including the two-turn case where a bare `done` repeats the previous turn's question — because send() already clears `curRaw` (line 530) so the stale-question collision cannot happen. The `|| ""` fallback on line 471 is dead as well: the server never emits an empty question (`question = result.output or "Could you clarify?"`, loop.py:291), and `|| ""` would make `askedThisTurn` falsy, which is the one value that silently disables the guard. Delete line 212, the assignment on 471 and the ` askedThisTurn = null;` fragment on the 530 chain (-2 lines); the whole fix then becomes the one-line condition in P1. Honest trade-off: `curRaw`'s comment says "raw text accumulated into curTextEl", so the guard reads as a coupling between rendering buffer and dedupe; if the owner prefers an explicitly named flag, `askedThisTurn = true` + `!askedThisTurn` is the smaller version of what shipped (drops the string payload and the null-check, keeps one global). Both are smaller than the current code; only the curRaw form is smallest.

quote: curTextEl = null; curRaw = ""; curToggle = null; curThink = null; toolGroup = null; askedThisTurn = null;
claim: No ordering hazard from appending to this chain: it is a flat sequence of independent assignments in one statement, executed before `addThinking()`/`busy = true` and before the fetch, so every frame of the turn is handled after the reset; nothing on the line reads another variable on the line. No newly dead member either — `toolGroup = null` is load-bearing (addTool only creates a row when `!toolGroup`, so without it a turn that opens with a tool would append into the previous turn's row), and `curRaw = ""` is what makes P2's deletion safe across turns (measured). The one item that becomes dead is this commit's own ` askedThisTurn = null;` fragment: once P2 lands it has nothing to reset, and `curRaw = ""` three tokens to its left is the reset the surviving code needs. Pre-existing, out of scope, worth only a note: `curToggle`/`curThink` are already re-nulled by `openText()` on every bubble creation (line 338) and are unreachable while `curTextEl` is null, so those two resets are subsumed — not touched here, this commit neither created nor worsened that.
